w: Mu.ZEE formed in 2008 from the merger of Ostend's modern art museum and its museum of fine arts, and now surveys Belgian art from 1830 onward - its name shortens 'Kunstmuseum aan Zee', Art Museum at the Sea. It also runs two satellite houses: the Ensorhuis, former home of James Ensor, and the Permekemuseum in Jabbeke.
s: Ensor's city, collected: Belgian art since 1830
_facts: Formed 2008 from merger of PMMK and Museum voor Schone Kunsten Oostende
Covers Belgian art from 1830 onward
Name abbreviates 'Kunstmuseum aan Zee'
Runs the Ensorhuis and the Permekemuseum as dependencies

w: Mercator is a steel-hulled barquentine launched in 1932 in Leith, Scotland, built to train the Belgian merchant fleet and named for cartographer Gerardus Mercator. Before the war she also worked as a research vessel and a floating ambassador at world fairs. Since 1964 she has sat as a museum ship in Ostend's marina.
s: 1932 training barquentine, now a floating museum
_facts: Steel-hulled barquentine launched 1932, built in Leith
Named after Gerardus Mercator
Used for scientific observation and as a world's-fair ambassador
Museum ship in Ostend's marina since 1964

w: The Hippodrome Wellington has staged flat and harness racing since 1883, named for the Duke of Wellington. Michael Jackson, Bowie and Bon Jovi have all played concerts here, Jackson's 1997 show dedicated to Princess Diana days after her death; its infield now doubles as a golf course.
s: 1883 racecourse where Michael Jackson played for Diana
_facts: Built 1883, named after the Duke of Wellington
Linked to the royal villa by the Royal Galleries
Hosted concerts by Michael Jackson (1997), Bowie (2002), Bon Jovi (2003)
Infield converted to a golf course in 2004

w: Near Raversijde, the Atlantic Wall Open Air Museum preserves over 60 bunkers and two miles of trenches, among the best-kept stretches of the German defensive line in Europe. They survived because they stood on land belonging to Prince Charles, Count of Flanders, who insisted they be kept as a monument, not demolished.
s: 60-plus WWII bunkers, saved by a prince's request
_facts: Over 60 bunkers and two miles of trenches
Among the best-preserved Atlantic Wall sections in Europe
Land owned by Prince Charles, Count of Flanders
Kept as a monument rather than demolished after WWII

w: The Japanese Garden of Ostend, also known as Shin Kai Tei - Deep Sea Garden in Japanese - was designed by the architect Takashi Sawano and opened in 2001 by Prince Philippe of Belgium. It is a formal Japanese-style park set down in the middle of this Belgian coastal city, a short walk from the North Sea shore.
s: Shin Kai Tei: a 'deep sea garden' opened by a prince
_facts: Designed by Takashi Sawano
Opened 2001 by Prince Philippe of Belgium
Name Shin Kai Tei translates as 'Deep Sea Garden'

w: The Royal Galleries of Ostend are a neoclassical arcade over 380 metres long, running the seafront dike from the royal villa to the Hippodrome Wellington racecourse. A pavilion anchors each end, and the Thermae Palace Hotel sits atop the middle, built so royalty could pass between villa and racetrack, rain or shine.
s: 380m arcade linking a king's villa to the races
_facts: Neoclassical arcade over 380 metres long
Runs from the royal villa to the Hippodrome Wellington
Thermae Palace Hotel sits atop the central section
